Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image appear to be a drawing made from chalk?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image as a whole has the appearance of a chalk-made drawing. Fail if it clearly does not have that appearance, including when it shows only an unrelated edit or a partial chalk effect. Unknown if the edited image is unavailable or the appearance cannot be determined.
node.binding: O1: Judge the edited image against the requested outcome of a chalk drawing; supporting evidence does not independently earn completion credit.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image has a visibly drawn, grainy, chalk-like texture across the giraffes and background, giving the image as a whole the appearance of a chalk drawing.

fulfillment: The node’s completion rule is too permissive: it treats a grainy, chalk-like texture as sufficient proof of a chalk-made drawing, and the trace consequently returns “yes” despite the reference being “partial.” Refine the binding and criteria to distinguish an overall chalk-drawing rendering from a photo that merely has a chalky overlay, while assessing the image as a whole and preserving the rubric’s partial-progress distinction. Here, the giraffes and scene remain recognizable, but the strong blur/smear and texture do not by themselves establish that the image has been rendered as a chalk drawing; the trace should not equate texture with completion. Keep the no-progress check available when completion is not established, and treat a conditional skip as unobserved—not as evidence either way. The high-confidence pass is a reason to inspect the criterion’s threshold and evidence interpretation, not to lower confidence mechanically or force the reference label.
